item.title: Honduras National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Honduras National Day

Press Statement

September 15, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I congratulate the people of Honduras as you celebrate your Independence Day.

This occasion honors the enduring principles of liberty and justice that continue to guide Honduras forward.  Honduras stands with us as a founding member of the Shield of the Americas, defending democratic sovereignty across our hemisphere.  Our nations share a partnership grounded in mutual respect and a commitment to the safety and prosperity of our citizens.  I commend President Nasry Asfura’s steadfast leadership in advancing our shared priorities of strengthening border security, disrupting transnational crime, and expanding economic opportunity for both of our peoples.

As Hondurans mark this proud day, the United States stands with you in pursuit of a more secure and prosperous future.

item.title: Nicaragua National Day
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Nicaragua National Day

Press Statement

September 15, 2026

On behalf of the United States of America, I send my solidarity to the Nicaraguan people on this day commemorating your independence. More than two centuries ago, Nicaraguans forged their own path to determine their future. Today, that same conviction endures despite the Murillo-Ortega dictatorship’s brutal efforts to annihilate it.

Whether at home or in exile, Nicaraguans’ aspirations for a future free from tyranny cannot be cancelled or erased.  The United States recognizes the Nicaraguan people’s strong resolve and conviction and today celebrates the ties that bind our two peoples.

item.title: United States Welcomes Djibouti’s Signing of the Artemis Accords
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

United States Welcomes Djibouti’s Signing of the Artemis Accords

Media Note

September 14, 2026

The Department of State congratulates the Republic of Djibouti on joining the Artemis Accords. Djibouti is the 72nd country to sign the Accords to date, pledging its commitment to the peaceful exploration of space.

Djibouti’s Ambassador to the United States Mohamed Siad Douale signed the Accords on behalf of the Republic of Djibouti on September 14, 2026. NASA Deputy Administrator Matthew Anderson and State Department Assistant Secretary for African Affairs Frank Garcia witnessed and celebrated the signing at a ceremony at the Mary W. Jackson NASA Headquarters in Washington, D.C. Djibouti most recently participated in the Department’s U.S.-Africa Technical and Regulatory Space Training Meeting in April 2026, and Djibouti’s first two satellites launched from Vandenberg Space Force Base in 2023 and 2024 respectively.

The United States and seven other countries established the Artemis Accords in 2020 to serve as a set of practical principles to guide responsible space exploration.  Djibouti joins the United States and 70 other nations in affirming the Accords’ principles for sustainable civil space activity. The Department of State and NASA lead the United States’ outreach and implementation of the Accords.

For more information, including a full list of signatories to the Accords, please visit  Artemis Accords.  For media inquiries, please submit a request.

item.title: U.S. Sanctions VTB Bank for Aiding Iran’s Sanctions Evasion
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

U.S. Sanctions VTB Bank for Aiding Iran’s Sanctions Evasion

Press Statement

September 14, 2026

The United States sanctioned VTB Bank, one of Russia’s largest financial institutions, for helping Iran evade sanctions and sustain its support for terrorism. VTB Bank opened offices in Iran, built banking ties with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions, and worked to move billions of dollars in Iranian assets.

The United States remains steadfast in cutting off the financial lifelines that allow the Iranian regime to fund terrorism, destabilize the region, and threaten U.S. economic security.

Today’s action sends a clear message to governments and financial institutions considering similar arrangements: any effort to help Iran evade sanctions will carry serious consequences, including exposure to U.S. financial restrictions.

The United States will continue to use every diplomatic and economic tool at its disposal to isolate the Iranian regime. We urge the international community to join this effort to sever the financial lifelines of a regime that threatens peace and security.

Today’s action is being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the financial sector of Iran’s economy and advances Operation Economic Outcast—a campaign to completely isolate the regime from the financial lifelines that sustain its malign behavior. Please see the Department of the Treasury’s Press Release.

item.title: Joint Statement on the Quad Tabletop Exercise in Tokyo to Advance Indo-Pacific Logistics Network
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Joint Statement on the Quad Tabletop Exercise in Tokyo to Advance Indo-Pacific Logistics Network 

Media Note

September 14, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of Japan, Australia, India, and the United States of America following the completion of a Tabletop Exercise (TTX) in Tokyo to advance the Quad Indo-Pacific Logistics Network (IPLN).

Begin Text:

On September 3 and 4, 2026, the Quad partners (Australia, India, Japan and the United States) conducted a Tabletop Exercise (TTX) in Tokyo, Japan to advance the Quad Indo-Pacific Logistics Network (IPLN) to enhance civilian response efforts across the region. The Ministry of Defense of Japan hosted the TTX, as concurred in the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in May 2026.

Building upon the results of the inaugural IPLN TTX in Hawai’i in April 2025 and the Field Training Exercise (FTX) in Guam in December 2025, this TTX focused on natural disaster response scenarios, through which Quad partners examined how best to leverage each partner’s logistics capabilities, while strengthening interoperability and streamlining coordination among the four partners. Through the TTX, the Quad partners made significant progress toward the development of the IPLN Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), which will provide an institutional framework for the effective operationalization of the IPLN.

Quad partners expressed their deepest condolences to all those affected by the recent devastating floods and underscored their shared commitment to supporting regional partners in times of need. They also discussed how best to coordinate humanitarian and relief efforts during crisis and emergency situations.

The IPLN is an initiative that enables Quad partners to leverage shared logistics capabilities to support civilian response to large-scale natural disasters more rapidly and efficiently across the Indo-Pacific to save lives, boost recovery efforts, and provide support for regional partners. This TTX reaffirmed the Quad’s unwavering commitment to strengthen practical cooperation to address regional challenges and to ensure a free and open Indo-Pacific. Quad partners will continue to make efforts to operationalize the IPLN, including through tabletop and field training exercises, confidence building measures, and subject matter expert exchanges.

End Text.

item.title: New U.S Health Partnership with Vietnam Under the Trump Administration’s America First Global Health Strategy
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

New U.S Health Partnership with Vietnam Under the Trump Administration’s America First Global Health Strategy

Press Statement

September 14, 2026

On September 11, the United States and Vietnam signed a five-year bilateral Health Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) under the Trump Administration’s America First Global Health Strategy (AFGHS), advancing our new model of co-investment in global health.

Through this MOU, the Department of State, working with Congress, plans to provide $98,750,000 in life-saving global health assistance over the next five years, including $21,385,000 in dedicated Global Health Security funding, to support Vietnam’s transition to full country ownership of its HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis programs while strengthening its capacity to detect and respond to emerging and re-emerging infectious disease threats. Vietnam is well-positioned to assume this responsibility and concurrent to this MOU, their annual health expenditure is projected to grow by approximately $10.5 billion over the five-year MOU period, from $23.3 billion to $33.8 billion. This five-year partnership ensures that the gains achieved through more than two decades of U.S. support are preserved, owned, and sustained by Vietnam’s own health institutions.

As Vietnam charts a new path for its health care system, this partnership is expected to deliver measurable results over the next five years. HIV and TB programming will fully transition to Vietnamese ownership within that period. Vietnam will move closer to its HIV epidemic-control targets through expanded prevention, case finding, and treatment, backed by greater domestic ownership and sustainability. Earlier detection and treatment of tuberculosis will reduce transmission, morbidity, and mortality, while lowering the risk of drug-resistant TB reaching the United States.

This new five-year phase of U.S.–Vietnam health cooperation builds on the strong foundation of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, complementing our robust ties in trade, security, and innovation. The America First Global Health Strategy reflects the Trump Administration’s commitment to protecting Americans from infectious disease threats, ending cycles of dependency, and building durable, country-led health systems around the world.

America First Global Health Strategy Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) signed so far represent more than $24.7 billion in new health funding, including more than $14.6 billion in U.S. assistance alongside more than $10.1 billion in co-investment from recipient countries, building on decades of progress fighting HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis, and other infectious diseases around the world. As of September 11, the State Department has signed 35 bilateral global health MOUs with Angola, Bolivia, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cambodia, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Guatemala, Guinea, Honduras, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mozambique, Niger, Nigeria, Panama, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Rwanda, Senegal, Sierra Leone, South Sudan, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Uganda, and Vietnam.

item.title: United States Approves Additional Funding for the Nepal Floods Response
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

United States Approves Additional Funding for the Nepal Floods Response

Media Note

September 12, 2026

The United States continues to extend our deepest sympathy to all those affected by the flooding in Nepal and their families, and we reaffirm our enduring friendship with the Nepali people. The safety of Americans in the affected area remains our highest priority. 

As part of our efforts to support the Nepal Government in identifying victims of the flood, the State Department’s Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs has approved $1 million to provide forensic support to Nepal Police. We are working closely with Nepal Police to identify the highest-priority needs, including DNA analysis kits. 

With this additional funding, the State Department has now provided over $5 million in humanitarian, health, and forensics-related assistance following the floods, including:

  •  $3 million in food and logistics assistance provided through our global assistance award with World Food Program.  This will provide up to three months of emergency food to 10,000 flood-affected households and address major supply chain constraints in humanitarian deliveries, by utilizing air and ground transport to reach communities cut off from access.

  • $685,000 in food, shelter, water, sanitation, and hygiene, protection, and financial assistance through our global assistance award with Catholic Relief Services (CRS). CRS is providing a range of U.S. Government-funded assistance to communities affected by the floods, including essential shelter and food items, blankets, plastic sheeting, tents, solar lights, and dignity kits, while also operating child-friendly spaces to support affected children. 

  • $365,000 in health, nutrition, and water, sanitation, and hygiene assistance to flood-affected communities through Jhpiego, FHI-360, and UNICEF.

FBI forensic specialists are also working alongside Nepal Police to support disaster victim identification and provide specialized humanitarian expertise, helping authorities identify victims and provide answers to families of American citizens and all victims of the tragedy.

 The U.S. military has delivered 5,000 specialized disaster victim recovery supplies, 500 first aid kits, stretchers, and front-end loaders to support Nepal-led search, rescue, and recovery operations. A four-person U.S. Military Civil Affairs Team is on the ground to conduct overseas humanitarian, disaster, and civic aid projects which will help address post-crisis humanitarian needs.   

This is a rapidly evolving operation, and we are working closely with our local partners on the ground to adapt to conditions as they change.  As the Secretary has reiterated, the United States is prepared to work closely with the Government of Nepal to continue to deliver additional assistance that responds directly to Nepal’s needs.  

For the latest information and resources related to our response, the Department created a dedicated Nepal Flash Floods Information webpage.

item.title: Strengthening U.S. Ties with the Pacific: Deputy Secretary Landau Engages Partners in Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Kiribati
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Strengthening U.S. Ties with the Pacific: Deputy Secretary Landau Engages Partners in Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Kiribati

Media Note

September 11, 2026

Fresh from his meetings with government partners at the Pacific Islands Forum in Palau, Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau traveled to the Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), Solomon Islands, and Kiribati to advance the Trump Administration’s America First economic and security priorities across the Pacific.

The Deputy Secretary reaffirmed our commitment to the FSM in a bilateral meeting with FSM President Wesley Simina. The Deputy Secretary also surveyed the recovery efforts following Typhoon Sinlaku’s damage in Chuuk State where he announced the United States intends to provide over $100 million to support disaster relief and reconstruction in FSM, delivering on U.S. commitments under the Compact of Free Association.

In Solomon Islands, the Deputy Secretary emphasized the bonds forged during World War II and outlined a vision for mutual progress in a free and open Pacific. He paid his respects at Guadalcanal, Red Beach, and Bloody Ridge Memorials where Americans, Solomon Islanders, and other Allied forces sacrificed their lives to turn the tide of the war. The Deputy Secretary announced U.S. support through the Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation for the preservation of the Bloody Ridge battlefield as a site of perpetual remembrance and continuing education. Looking forward, he signed an agreement with Minister for Foreign Affairs and External Trade Rick Houenipwela for the Peace Corps to return to the Solomon Islands after a 26-year absence. At Honiara Airport, he concluded his visit by announcing that the U.S. Department of State, working with Congress, intends to provide four aircraft rescue and firefighting vehicles to enhance the safety of American and international tourists. He also announced the Millenium Challenge Corporation will conduct a condition assessment to determine the cost of rehabilitating the Solomon Islands Parliament.

In Kiribati, the Deputy Secretary attended the Kiribati Development Partners Forum on Kiritimati Island at the invitation of President Taneti Maamau to emphasize U.S. commitment to partnership with Kiribati on economic development in line with the Kiribati 20-Year Vision. The Deputy Secretary announced the Millenium Challenge Corporation will conduct a study to update and expand the wharf on Kiritimati Island. This initiative will lay the foundation for a long-term infrastructure investment to increase access to trade and support maritime security and combatting illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing for the peoples of Kiritimati.

Throughout the visit, the Deputy Secretary reaffirmed the United States’ longstanding commitment to partnering with Pacific Island nations to expand economic and commercial opportunities, strengthen digital connectivity, combat transnational criminal activity, and safeguard global health security. Meeting with senior leaders in each country, he unveiled new initiatives to advance a free and open Pacific, expand opportunities for U.S. businesses, and deliver concrete economic results for the American taxpayer.

item.title: U.S. Takes Action Against Iran’s Terrorist Proxies
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

U.S. Takes Action Against Iran’s Terrorist Proxies

Press Statement

September 10, 2026

Today, the United States is taking action under Operation Economic Outcast targeting Kata’ib Hizballah (KH), Hizballah, and the broader financial networks that sustain Iran’s campaign of regional destabilization. These groups serve as Tehran’s instruments for projecting violence and subversion across the Middle East and the globe, threatening the security of Iraq, Lebanon, the safety of American personnel and diplomatic facilities in the region, and global energy flows. KH, designated a Foreign Terrorist Organization by the State Department in 2009, has intensified its threat to U.S. interests, including a recent plot to attack Jewish institutions in the United States, and continues to direct attacks against U.S. and Coalition forces in Iraq that endanger innocent civilians and undermine Iraqi sovereignty.

The actions announced today expose the extent to which Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps–Qods Force (IRGC-QF) has co-opted Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces and exploited commercial networks in Iraq, the UAE, Türkiye, and Lebanon to fund terrorism and evade international sanctions.

The United States remains committed to supporting a sovereign, stable Iraq free from malign external influence, and to protecting Lebanon’s institutions from Hizballah’s corrosive financial and political interference. These networks not only threaten regional stability but also undermine the economic interests of the very populations Iran claims to serve.

The United States will continue working closely with partners across the region and around the world to isolate Iran’s terrorist proxies and disrupt the financial lifelines that enable their operations.

Today’s action is being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended, which targets terrorists and their supporters, and E.O. 13902, which targets certain sectors of the Iranian economy. This action advances Operation Economic Outcast—a campaign to completely isolate the regime from the financial lifelines that sustain its malign behavior. Please see the Department of the Treasury’s Press Release.

These groups serve as Tehran’s instruments for projecting violence and subversion across the Middle East and the globe, threatening the security of Iraq, Lebanon, the safety of American personnel and diplomatic facilities in the region, and global energy flows. KH, designated a Foreign Terrorist Organization by the State Department in 2009, has intensified its threat to U.S. interests, including a recent plot to attack Jewish institutions in the United States, and continues to direct attacks against U.S. and Coalition forces in Iraq that endanger innocent civilians and undermine Iraqi sovereignty.

The actions announced today expose the extent to which Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps–Qods Force (IRGC-QF) has co-opted Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces and exploited commercial networks in Iraq, the UAE, Türkiye, and Lebanon to fund terrorism and evade international sanctions.

The United States remains committed to supporting a sovereign, stable Iraq free from malign external influence, and to protecting Lebanon’s institutions from Hizballah’s corrosive financial and political interference. These networks not only threaten regional stability but also undermine the economic interests of the very populations Iran claims to serve.

The United States will continue working closely with partners across the region and around the world to isolate Iran’s terrorist proxies and disrupt the financial lifelines that enable their operations.

Today’s action is being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended, which targets terrorists and their supporters, and E.O. 13902, which targets certain sectors of the Iranian economy. This action advances Operation Economic Outcast—a campaign to completely isolate the regime from the financial lifelines that sustain its malign behavior. Please see the Department of the Treasury’s Press Release.

item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Quito, Ecuador

Palacio de Carondelet

Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the National Order of Merit in the Grade of Grand Cross Ceremony

Remarks

September 9, 2026

MODERATOR:  (Via interpreter) Good afternoon.  With your authorization, Mr. President, we will begin with the ceremony of the decoration at the grade of Grand Cross for the Order of National Merit to Mr. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America; reading the executive decree of the conferral of the decoration of the Order of Merit, the order of Grand Cross, to Mr. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States. 

FOREIGN MINISTER KURY:  (Via interpreter) Executive decree 492, issued by Mr. Daniel Noboa Azín, President of the Republic: Considering that according to Article 416 of the constitution of the republic establish that the interest of the presidents of the republic will respond to the interest of the international community, and hereby decrees that integration, cooperation, and solidarity; that with (inaudible) 391 of September 17, 1920 – 2026  issued for the Order of Merit, created of – in this year, is of Article 6 of (inaudible) 0924 of 17 – of September 17, 2026 – determined that Mr. President of the Republic, through the Ministry of the Foreign Affairs, establish the way the conferral of decoration must be done.   

That executive decree of September 17, 2026 established that within the numerals of Article 26 have to be the minimal requirements for the conferral of decoration without prejudice; that in each case the Ministry of Foreign Affairs determines the possibility of its conferral according to the merits and the background of each candidate.  Article 8 of executive decree 2026 – of 17 September 2026, establish the reasons that are not established within these numerals will be decided by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs that is contained within the list above, according to the order and merits.   

This is an order established by the Ecuadorian state for people with a high trajectory of work and with the cooperation and friendship relations with international community in benefits of security, development, and the security of its peoples. 

Mr. Marco Antonio Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America, has been providing distinguished services and has done high commitment to the bonds of friendship with the Republic of Ecuador and the United States; contributed within his high functions the consolidation of a bilateral relation based on trust, cooperation, and the achievement of mutual interest; and also strengthening bilateral cooperation to face, in a coordinated way, threats coming from the transnational organized crime, in particularly narco-traffic, narco-terrorism, and networks linked to illicit economies and their funds, thus fighting against the insecurity for these institutionally and development of the Republic of Ecuador.  His efforts for strengthening bilateral cooperation and security, strengthen institutional capabilities, and fight against illicit economies has contributed to have mutual agenda that has transcended these national borders, reaffirming the commitment of both countries for security, peace, stability, and the benefits of its peoples.   

And within the attributions conferred within the articles above mentioned, of article of September 17, 2026 decrees – hereby decrees to confer decoration to merit in the Order of Grand Cross to Mr. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America, for his distinguished services and his strengthening of the links of friendship, cooperation between the Republic of Ecuador and the United States of America. 

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is here charged to execute this executive decree and the organization of the political meeting that is here, and this decree will enter into force without prejudice of its publication in official registry; given at the National Palace on September 9th, 2026, signed by Mr. Daniel Noboa Azín. 

(Applause.) 

MODERATOR:  (Via interpreter) Thank you, Mr. Minister of Foreign Affairs.  Hereby the imposition of the decoration in the Order of National Merit, in the grade of Grand Cross, to Mr. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America, imposed by Mr. Daniel Noboa Azín, Constitutional President of the Republic. 

(The medal was presented.) 

MODERATOR:  (Via interpreter) Now, words of Mr. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America. 

SECRETARY RUBIO:  (Via interpreter) First, thank you so much. This is a great honor for me. I’m going to go back to Washington wearing this. I’m honored to come back to visit all of you here. I was here recently and the relations with the United States and Ecuador have improved in the last years and specifically in the last three or four years, the cooperation we have on the issue of security and on the issue of prosperity, because both issues are important. 

However, the main goal of the government, it’s the security of this people, and when we see threats to its security, we have to work, and your president’s doing so in an incredible way.  And we have seen that in every single work that we have done together.  We have the same principles, and that is why we will continue to see a strong commitment on part of President Trump and our administration to help you all to continue working. 

At the same time, security is space for prosperity, that wants every government to have prosperity for its people, that have economic opportunities based on the help of the presidents and the authorities.  So let us all know that we are here, again, at the second time, and it’s the third time that I’ve met with the president – once before in the United States – to continue showing the cooperation and the links that are between our two countries. 

And I once again thank you so much for this, and thank you, all of you, for being here, for receiving me and working with me and my team.  And I don’t need a prize for this work; however, it is great honor to receive this.  So thank you so much.  (Applause.) 

MODERATOR:  (Via interpreter) Thank you, Mr. Secretary.  Now, the speech of Mr. Daniel Noboa Azin, Constitutional President of the Republic. 

PRESIDENT NOBOA:  (Via interpreter) Mr. Secretary of State, in the name of the Ecuadoran people, it is the honor of us to confer the decoration in the Order of Grand Cross to the merit, the equivalent of the presidential conferral decoration in the United States.  It’s not only for issue of security (inaudible) and policies and social works, but also in the culture.  The details of – I’m always happy of both decorations, and in this last part, I would like to highlight, because what we will continue doing with Mr. Secretary Rubio is take care in preserving the culture of the American continent, saving its values, and giving peace not only for the United States but all the entire region. 

With this same strength and drive with which he’s working in his congressional hearings, he goes through every country to improve the livelihood of the peoples looking for security, safety, and also helping the United States to have a real connection not only at the level of governments but with its people.  That makes him a different secretary of what’s normally.  He’s special.  Moreover, that is known worldwide, that he’s solved many problems that are hard to solve.  There he is, Mr. Marco Rubio, solving each problem, knowing that even if that problem doesn’t have a solution, Mr. Marco Rubio will find a solution.  (Applause.)   

He has led very differently of what’s normal.  That makes him to have a good relation of the United States to the world and highlights also his roots and the connection with Latin America.  We, from the part of Ecuador, we are always thankful with his work, his service, and we have achieved working hand in hand with the United States to provide more peace, health, and also more liberties, not only for our peoples but also for the entire continent. 

Once again, I would like to repeat that it’s an honor for me to grant this decoration, the highest that Ecuador has here in Ecuador, and I hope to have him many times here in Ecuador visiting us, and also accompanying us with this fight to change the continent, and it’s for once, for all.  Thank you so much.  (Applause.)
